about: Edition 9 of storm-charles.promptugal.news's decision brief on Storm Charles: the words and judgements of this edition (the lead, what to watch, the authorities' decisions, sources compared). The figures (warnings, observations, flights, notices) are drawn by tools/brief-make.mjs from the incident's data files as they stood at the as-of time. Every item is labelled fact, evidence or hypothesis and carries its source and the time read. Not a warning service: IPMA issues the warnings and ANEPC the instructions.
next: After 21:00, when Lisbon's last warning above yellow (the orange sea) ends: an "after the storm" edition, forecast beside observations; or earlier at a new IPMA message.

lead.label: fact
lead.text: No red warning remains on the mainland: at 15:56 IPMA lowered Faro's red rain to yellow and its red wind to orange (to 18:00), and ended Lisbon's orange wind early (it ran to 18:00). Lisbon now: yellow rain to 18:00 and orange sea to 21:00, then yellow sea to 03:00. The government's alert situation runs to 23:59. Lower levels, not an all-clear.

src.name: IPMA's CAP messages sent 15:55:03 via MeteoAlarm (read 16:09, timeline s-1111T1609)

lead.label: fact
lead.text: Lisbon's storm in figures, as observed: the heaviest hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations was 26.2 mm at Oeiras (hour 13:00), about 73 mm in six hours at Oeiras and Relógio; the strongest gust at the airport 74 km/h at 14:00, below IPMA's orange threshold. At 15:00 the airport had south-south-west 41 km/h gusting 61, pressure 989 hPa, no rain.

lead.label: hypothesis
lead.text: The centre has most likely passed just north of Lisbon; the wind should turn west to north-west as the pressure rises. With the wind warning lifted early, the sea is Lisbon's last warning to 21:00: the coast and the riverside are where it still counts.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Lisbon's, Setúbal's and Beja's orange wind ended early; Faro's red rain and red wind lowered: no red left on the mainland.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Lisbon: yellow rain; orange sea to 21:00. Faro: yellow rain and orange wind to 18:00.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: TAF: wind turning west-north-west 12 kt by 18:00, no significant weather.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Yellow rain ends in Lisbon, Faro, Santarém and Leiria; Faro's orange wind ends; orange rain ends in Beja, Castelo Branco, Portalegre and Évora.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: TAF: at times west-north-west 17 kt gusting 27 (50 km/h).

watch.label: fact
watch.text: The orange sea ends in Lisbon, Setúbal, Beja and Faro; yellow sea (waves 4 to 5 m) to 03:00 Thursday. Lisbon's last warning above yellow ends.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: No IPMA warning for Lisbon above yellow on Thursday morning. IPMA's model: west wind, mean 15 to 24 km/h; showers, rain chance up to 92%.
watch.src: IPMA warnings and IPMA's hourly model (run 07:56)

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: Web Summit reported reopening for its last day (the press relaying the organisers' message to participants); which sessions move, the PITCH semi-final and tickets still unannounced.

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: The Interior Ministry says the alert situation ends today and expects normality to resume on Thursday (Lusa, 14:46; the government's order covered 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November).

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: The airport's wind turning west to north-west with the pressure rising (989 hPa at 14:00, still falling) would mean the centre has passed; the strongest gusts may come in that turn.

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: Thunderstorm cells (TCU or CB in the METAR) and wind shear at the airport, as at 14:00: the short, sharp spells are the ones to watch, not a long blow.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon's, Setúbal's and Beja's orange wind ended early at 15:56; Faro's red rain lowered to yellow and red wind to orange, to 18:00. No red warning remains on the mainland.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Rain lowered from red to yellow in Santarém and from orange to yellow in Leiria, 15:06 to 18:00; no message for Lisbon. Only Faro remains under red.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon's red rain warning ended at 15:00 as its 12:33 messages set it; yellow rain and orange wind to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: The alert situation ends today; normality expected to resume on Thursday.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon urban trains suppressed between Campolide and Alcântara Terra; four Intercidades over the 25 de Abril bridge suppressed in the most critical hours, no replacement buses; refund or free exchange for long-distance and regional tickets.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Day 3 reopens on Thursday 12 November, "the busiest Thursday ever"; some of Wednesday's sessions move to Thursday. Reported by 24 Notícias and Público from the organisers' message to participants; not read at the organisers' own page.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon's warnings shortened (CAP, nine messages): red rain 12:34–15:00, then yellow to 18:00; orange wind to 18:00; Setúbal the same for rain, orange wind to 18:00; Beja orange wind to 18:00; Santarém and Leiria yellow wind to 18:00.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Trafaria – Porto Brandão – Belém: vehicle transport interrupted for weather and sea; passengers only between Porto Brandão and Belém; no forecast for Trafaria.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Since 11:30, a maximum of 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril bridge and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama, for heavy rain and poor visibility; motorcycles and wind-prone vehicles advised against crossing; may change at any moment.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Communiqué no. 3: Charles split into two centres; wind weaker than forecast yesterday; gusts 70 to 90 km/h in the South, up to 110 km/h exposed; "the warnings were adjusted".

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Alert situation for the whole mainland, Wednesday 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services closed; outdoor events suspended.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Day 2 (Wednesday) will not take place, on the government's formal advice; Day 3 (Thursday) "aims to proceed as planned".

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: All of Lisbon's road tunnels closed from midnight; parks, gardens and cultural facilities too.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Service kept with priority to essential journeys; trams 12E, 15E, 18E, 24E, 25E and 28E interrupted; Graça funicular closed since 10:40; Web Summit shuttles cancelled. Fertagus trains: normal service, confirmed at 10:40.
decided.when: read 11:52 at source (no update time on the page)

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: River crossings between Lisbon and the south bank kept running from 05:00 (one crossing, Porto Brandão–Trafaria–Belém, reported suspended in the morning).

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Operations adjusted; tickets for travel to 11 Nov may be changed without penalty to flights up to 17 Nov.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Wednesday's scheduled activity rescheduled (which hospitals: not stated).

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Schools closed Wednesday morning, reopening from 13:00. 205 occurrences to 09:00, none classed as serious.

compare.models: TAF: rain all afternoon, heavy with a 30% thunderstorm chance 12:00–16:00
compare.obs: Heaviest hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations in our record: 26.2 mm Oeiras (hour 13:00); about 73 mm in six hours at Oeiras and Relógio
compare.press: SAPO titles "particularly intense rain between 15:00 and 18:00" (which region: not stated in the title; not checked)
compare.assessment: The red warning matched the heaviest rain of the storm in Lisbon; for the afternoon IPMA's word is yellow, at times heavy, not a new red.

compare.official: No red left: Faro red to yellow at 15:56; Santarém red to yellow, Leiria orange to yellow at 15:06
compare.models: Communiqué no. 3: rain moving south-west to north-east
compare.obs: n/a in our data (our station table is Lisbon's)
compare.press: ECO: "eight districts in red" (the earlier count; not what the 12:18 batch says)
compare.assessment: Read the CAP messages, not the headline: four districts in red rain.

compare.official: Orange ended early at 15:56 (was to 18:00), CAP 15:55
compare.models: TAF lowered twice: at times 65 km/h gusts, 30% chance of 102 km/h in thunderstorms; ECMWF ensemble gusts at Lisbon: median 69, 90th percentile 85 km/h
compare.obs: Strongest gust 74 km/h at 14:00; 61 km/h at 15:00, south-south-west
compare.press: Weather.com still headlines the red wind warning IPMA withdrew at 07:16
compare.assessment: The wind peaked as the centre passed, below the orange threshold; IPMA lifted the warning two hours early.

compare.official: Warnings overlap 12:00–18:00 (red rain, orange wind, orange sea)
compare.assessment: The early afternoon, to about 16:00, is the window the sources share; the peak hour within it is not known.

compare.official: Communiqué no. 3 (12:16): two centres; less deepening
compare.models: ECMWF ensemble (51 forecasts): 49% south of Lisbon, 41% near, 10% north; median crossing about 15:00
compare.obs: Wind turned east to south in 30 minutes at 14:00, temperature up 2 °C, pressure 989 hPa
compare.press: Track moved south, toward the Algarve (radio, 10:38; not IPMA in writing)
compare.assessment: Passing just north of Lisbon (our meteorologist's analysis 21, revising "just south"); the ensemble had 41% near, 10% north.

compare.official: Orange sea, 12:00–21:00: waves 5–7 m, up to 13 m; yellow to 03:00
compare.models: IPMA's model: sea 3–3.5 m Thursday morning; tide model: high water about 15:10 (1.25 m), next about 03:10 Thursday
compare.obs: No gauge or buoy in our data; Instituto Hidrográfico's official table needs an account (not read)
compare.press: Rain at high tide may hinder drainage (live blog, 08:27)
compare.assessment: High water about 15:10 has come with the yellow rain; the orange sea warning stands to 21:00.

compare.official: Lowered to yellow and green on IPMA's warnings page (12:24); earlier red rain to 06:00, orange wind to 12:00
compare.obs: 249.5 mm in six hours at Areeiro (01:00–06:00); airport wind dropped from 89 km/h gusts at 07:00 to 13 km/h at 08:00
compare.press: Regional president: 479 mm somewhere on the island; 205 occurrences, none serious
compare.assessment: The worst has passed Madeira; the risk now is what the rain left (slopes, streams), which only the regional civil protection can state.

compare.official: Lisbon: yellow rain to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00, yellow sea to 03:00; no red on the mainland since 15:56
compare.models: TAF: no significant weather from about 18:00; showers on Thursday
compare.press: Interior Ministry: the alert situation ends today, normality expected Thursday (Lusa); Web Summit reported reopening
compare.assessment: The end is in IPMA's own windows: 18:00 for wind and rain, 21:00 for the sea.

No red warning remains on the mainland. Lisbon now: yellow rain to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00, yellow sea to 03:00. ana: Lisbon airport: 565 movements scheduled for the day, 288 cancelled in advance by airlines and 22 more by 11:00 (Madeira 20 of 80 cancelled in advance, Faro 14 of 62, Porto 12 of 214), from the airports' operator's own newsroom, situation at 11:00.
grid_note: IPMA's file now starts every re-issued warning at 12:34, so the hours before are not drawn: Lisbon's red rain was in force from 09:00, its orange wind from 09:00 and its orange sea from 12:00 (editions 1 to 6 show them).
